newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Troika stands by mideast fact-finding visit.
newsitem.headline: Troika stands by mideast fact-finding visit.

text.p: The European Union said on Wednesday that it was trying to set dates for a fact-finding visit to the Middle East to get the peace process back on track.
Ireland, the current EU President, said in a statement that the peace process was at a "critical juncture" and a troika of EU ministers planned to visit the region.
The troika consists of the past, present and next EU presidents.

It quoted Gay Mitchell, European Affairs minister, as saying the mission "will seek to provide reassurance to Israel aand the Arab states of the Union's intention to contribute to getting the process back on track."
The statement left open the question as to whether the troika would seek to hold talks with the Palestinian Authority in Orient House in disputed East Jerusalem.
The Israeli government has said it would disapprove strongly of such a visit and maintains that Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat has switched his political offices from Orient House to elsewhere.
An EU Foreign Affairs meeting in Tralee, southern Ireland, last month said it would discuss the venue for such a meeting with Arafat and his aides.
The statement was made in an announcement of an extra 20 million Ecus of aid after violence flared between Palestinians and Israelis last week.
Arafat appealed for aid after dozens of people were killed and injured in violence which erupted over the building of a tunnel in part of Jerusalem sacred to Moslems and Jews.
